subject: Zenbridge hybrid handoff - sticky translation & intermittent uploads
messages:
From: Liz Howard <liz.howard@zenbridge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya@zenbridge.com>, ops@zenbridge.com
Date: 2026-05-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent upload failures after hybrid gateway handoff

Hi Rafael,

We started the hybrid handoff to Redwood Private yesterday evening (staged cutover). Since then our nightly bulk uploads to the analytics bucket have failed intermittently — usually around the 10MB-30MB mark, but sometimes at ~150MB. The failures look like TCP connection resets from our side and the files show up as truncated on S3.

We ran a quick traceroute and attached a tcpdump from one of the failing hosts. Key observations:
- Most client connections complete the TLS handshake and begin sending, then stall and the sender closes with RST after ~18s.
- Some flows succeed if retried immediately; others consistently fail until we clear the local conntrack table.
- Our infra team suspects NAT ephemeral port exhaustion or an MSS/MTU issue with the new edge.

Can your team help triage? We have a maintenance window at 0100 UTC tonight where we can enable additional logging or adjust MSS clamp if needed.

Thanks,
Liz
Liz Howard
Head of Platform Engineering, Zenbridge Health
Attachment: tcpdump-zenbridge-0518.pcap (pcap, 4.2MB)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Liz Howard <liz.howard@zenbridge.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@zenbridge.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent upload failures after hybrid gateway handoff

Vanessa / Marissa / Karthik — looping you in.

Initial read: pcap shows lots of established flows that transfer data and then we see a burst of retransmits followed by a client RST. There are also a handful of SYN->SYN-ACK->ACK flows where the server's TCP MSS is ~1460 and some segments show [TCP segment of a reassembled PDU] which suggests possible fragmentation further down the path.

Hypotheses:
1) Conntrack state exhaustion or port reuse on the hybrid NAT path causing late RSTs.
2) MTU > Path MTU (PMTUD blackhole) with TLS pushing large segments that get dropped — TCP then stalls and app times out.
3) Security group or stateful firewall on the customer's edge is dropping mid-flow packets after a translation bounce.

Ask: can Karthik validate conntrack counts and ephemeral port reservation on the private edge VMs (staging pool) and check whether we have any NAT timeouts configured unusually low? Vanessa / Marissa, can you review the edge security group logs for any DROP events around the timestamps in the pcap?

I'll request a short maintenance slot from Zenbridge for 01:00 UTC to run an MSS clamp test and to temporarily increase conntrack table size on a canary host.

- Raf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Liz Howard <liz.howard@zenbridge.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@zenbridge.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent upload failures after hybrid gateway handoff

Quick checks from the staging NAT cluster:
- Conntrack usage spiked from ~6,200 to ~62,000 on 2026-05-17 23:40 UTC (matches cutover window) with table hash collisions observed on host nat-stg-03. We are currently at 67k (soft limit 70k).
- Ephemeral port exhaustion not yet reached, but port reuse rate is high for short-lived flows (high churn).
- NAT timeouts: default 30s for established TCP on our ring; some uploads are long-lived (60s+). That mismatch could cause mid-transfer translation eviction if flows idle briefly.
- MTU checks: edge devices show MTU 1500; we see a couple of ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages in the pcap but they don't have clear source IPs — likely ICMP being rate-limited by an intermediate.

Immediate mitigations I can apply to a canary host during the maintenance window:
- bump conntrack limit to 200k and tune hashsize to reduce collisions.
- temporarily extend established TCP timeout to 300s.
- enable MSS clamp at 1380 for the staging NAT interface.

I will coordinate with Rafael and Zenbridge on the exact host. Also recommend a short traceroute with DF set from a failing host to surface PMTUD blackholes (we can script that).

Karthik
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Liz Howard <liz.howard@zenbridge.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent upload failures after hybrid gateway handoff

Marissa ran the SG (security group) logs for the window Liz provided. Findings:
- No explicit DENY for established TCP flows in the SG attached to the sandbox cluster (sg-zenbridge-stg).
- Observed several flow termination events where the return path packets had a different source IP (translation bounce). Those sessions were permitted but the flow trace shows asymmetric return path via a partner exchange point.
- Also found repeated TCP RSTs coming from the original client IP shortly after a burst of retransmits — consistent with the client's OS aborting the socket after long retries.

Next steps (proposed during tonight's window):
1) Karthik will apply conntrack/table tunings + MSS clamp on nat-stg-03 (canary).
2) Rafael will add a temporary high-fidelity packet mirror to a collector for live inspection.
3) Zenbridge to run DF traceroutes and a small synthetic upload test with retries disabled so we can reproduce the exact failure timing.

If that doesn't resolve, we'll escalate to cross-network team to instrument the transit and confirm whether asymmetric return routes are breaking stateful expectations.

- Vanessa
From: Liz Howard <liz.howard@zenbridge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent upload failures after hybrid gateway handoff

Thanks all — update after the maintenance slot:
- We ran the DF traceroute and reproduced a fragment-drop between the customer edge and Redwood staging NAT (ICMP 'frag needed' without mtu in reply).
- After Karthik applied MSS clamp=1380 and conntrack bump on nat-stg-03, our synthetic uploads completed at >99% success for a 2-hour window.
- One remaining case: a subset of hosts behind a partner appliance still saw RSTs. We found the partner was performing a second NAT with a shorter TCP timeout (45s) and aggressive conntrack pruning. They've opened a change to align timeouts.

We appreciate the quick turnaround. Please keep the canary tunings in place for 72 hours and we'll monitor.

Action items captured in JIRA ZB-4127. I attached the packet capture and the updated topology for reference.

Best,
Liz

Attachment: zenbridge-topology-v2.png, tcpdump-zenbridge-0518.pcap, zenbridge-handoff-runbook.md
